doc: Gil's hand-keyed clips (art/wardens/gil/gil.glb, tools/art1/gil_clips.py) and which game state plays which (scripts/heroes/warden_clips.gd). The swordfish is skinned to hand.R in the .glb: the procedural swordfish (HeroArmsGil) hides and the Gun node is only the invisible aim and FX reference, kept on the blade empties (anchor_blade_root on hand.R, weapon_muzzle at the bill tip) so thrusts, potions and the spout leave the weapon you see. The Fencer thrusts take the whole body standing; while the lunge slides him, the legs keep the run under them (upper: moving), and so does the Grab Bag toss. Ground Swim's dive is the rig's keyed pose (KMovesGil gil_dive: the whole body under the ground; the swim clip only sinks him to the fin) and the surfacing is a clip; the Tidal Wave surf holds its loop (hold_from) until the kit plays the landing; Riptide's twirl is one clip through the longest spin.
